A letter from the U.S. Department of Justice went to Congressman Louis Stokes about the House Select Committee on Assassinations report. Stokes had chaired the committee, which reopened the Kennedy and King cases in the late 1970s. The department wrote to tell him the results of its own review of the committee's report.

Such letters close the loop between an inquiry and the department it examines. The committee had judged the Justice Department's earlier work, and now the department answered on paper. The letter preserves that official response, part of the long paper argument over how the assassinations were investigated.
hygienic-physiology-with-special-referen:
Joel Dorman Steele's Hygienic Physiology teaches the science of the human body, with attention to drink and drugs. The book is a new, longer version of his Fourteen Weeks in Human Physiology, made for schools under the drink-teaching laws then spreading across America.

Steele's Pathfinder series served young, middle and older pupils, and this third book was aimed at the oldest group. Skilled writers made the series for the science office of the Woman's Christian Temperance Union, and chosen readings back up the lessons. Readers keen on Victorian health teaching, or on how the drink reform cause entered the classroom, will find Steele clear, earnest and true to his time.
